title: Collect all the errors
prompt:
Implement `validate_user(payload)` returning `(clean, errors)`:

- `name`: required non-empty string → stored stripped
- `email`: required string containing '@' → stored stripped and lowercased
- `age`: int 0..150 — a digit-string like `'42'` is coerced to int first (bools are NOT ints here)
- every other key in the payload produces an `{'field': k, 'detail': 'unknown field'}` error, sorted by field name
- each error is `{'field': ..., 'detail': ...}`; when errors is non-empty, `clean` may only contain fields that passed

The final error list is sorted by field name.

The contract: report ALL problems in one call (collect, don't abort at the first).

tests.name: valid payload normalizes
tests.code:
clean, errors = validate_user({'name': '  Lan ', 'email': ' Lan@Example.COM ', 'age': '42'})
assert errors == []
assert clean == {'name': 'Lan', 'email': 'lan@example.com', 'age': 42}
print('ok')
tests.hint: Strip and case-fold before checking; coerce digit strings.

tests.name: every problem reported exactly once
tests.code:
clean, errors = validate_user({'name': 'Lan', 'email': 'nope', 'age': 999, 'extra': 1, 'zz': 2})
assert clean == {'name': 'Lan'}
fields = [e['field'] for e in errors]
assert fields == ['age', 'email', 'extra', 'zz'], fields
missing = validate_user({})
assert [e['field'] for e in missing[1]] == ['age', 'email', 'name']
print('ok')
tests.hint: One pass, every field checked, unknowns sorted by name.
